absent: Derivation of inner transport offset, inner TCP header length, head length, checksum offsets, and queue mapping inputs.
Behavior of transmit helpers for fragment handling, timestamping, descriptor construction, queue-full handling, kick and notification, and polling scheduling.
Receive helpers for descriptor refill, polling control, moderation handling, buffer release, and packet pool management.
Virtqueue backend operations for descriptor queueing, completion retrieval, broken-state detection, callback control, unused-buffer detachment, and transport-specific resize and affinity.
Control command encodings, status codes beyond success, device-side effects, and timing guarantees.
Receive-side scaling header and trailer layouts, size calculations, key handling, and hash versus scaling semantics.
Queue-pair enable and disable, configuration work scheduling, carrier control, and address-change validation and commit.
VLAN protocol argument use, upper-layer address-list synchronization, and routing protection scope beyond these fragments.
Allocation failure paths, error-code mappings for queue operations, and statistics protection details.
Interrupt, polling weight, moderation, and affinity hint lifecycle outside pause resume and cleanup.

findings.text: Ring sizing, affinity delegation, and configuration callback suppression are provided as shared services for network queue management and driver state control.

Transmit entry selects the queue indicated by the packet, reclaims or suspends completion handling according to polling mode, drops on fragment handling failure, timestamps, attempts descriptor setup with warning and drop on unexpected failure, detaches upper-layer state when not polling, applies queue-full control, and conditionally notifies the device with delayed callback rearm and polling scheduling.

Header construction from a packet initially clears the destination, then for segmented packets derives expected linear length and segment size, maps stack offload kinds for TCP over IP in distinct address families and UDP segmentation with an ECN extension bit and rejects unknown offload, selects no offload otherwise, and encodes partial checksum with VLAN-adjusted start and offset versus validated checksum versus neither.
Tunnel header length starts from the inner transport offset and adds UDP header size for UDP segmentation or inner TCP header size otherwise, stored in device byte order.
Ring resize rejects requests larger than the device maximum and rejects empty size requests, and returns success immediately when the requested size already equals the current size.

Generic resize drains unused buffers through a caller recycle routine, invokes an optional completion callback, performs backend size change, then re-enables the queue, propagating re-enable failure when it occurs in preference to the backend result. Drain stage requires caller ownership and presence of transport disable and enable operations, and re-enable failure is reported as busy.

Receive pause halts polling and cancels moderation when the interface is running, with a variant covering all possible pairs. Resume optionally prefills descriptors then re-enables polling when running, with a variant prefilling only active pairs. Resize stages temporary packet storage for growth, pauses, invokes backend resize with buffer release, adopts new storage only if size actually grew, reports failures, and resumes with refill.

Transmit pause disables completion polling when running, then under per-queue transmit protection marks reset, stops the subqueue, and counts the event. Resume clears the mark and wakes the queue under the same protection then re-enables polling when running. Resize rejects sizes at or below fragment count plus a small constant margin, then performs pause, backend resize with buffer release callbacks, and resume while reporting failures.
Control transactions are serialized by a dedicated mutex held across status initialization, descriptor assembly, queueing, notification, response polling, and success evaluation.
Transmit reset marking and subqueue stop and wake transitions are ordered under per-queue transmit bottom-half protection against concurrent transmission and polling access.

Configuration callback suppression is guarded by interrupt-safe spin protection around a flag. Receive-mode updates hold routing configuration protection across command issuance and address-list protection across unicast and multicast counting and copying.

Control transaction requires control queue support, assembles a bounded descriptor set with command header plus optional output plus mandatory status plus optional input, queues and notifies, then polls for completion or broken state with scheduling and relaxation, judging success by device-written status.

Address change rejects standby mode, duplicates the proposed address for validation, prefers a control command when supported, otherwise writes bytes through device configuration for legacy devices lacking version negotiation with acknowledged weak atomicity, then commits the change.

Statistics sum per-pair transmit and receive packet and byte counters plus transmit timeout and receive drop counters under sequence protection, supplemented by device-wide drop and error counters for transmit drops and FIFO errors and receive length and frame errors.

Queue-pair count update returns immediately without control support, otherwise when scaling is active without user customization it reallocates header storage, refreshes the indirection table and transmit queue limit, commits combined configuration with restoration on failure, and otherwise issues a dedicated count command, keeping the trailer limit synchronized and scheduling receive polling when up.
Scaling commit sends header and trailer as a paired scatter list using the scaling configuration variant when scaling is present and the hash configuration variant otherwise, warning on failure.
Close suppresses configuration callbacks, synchronously cancels configuration work, disables every queue pair while cancelling moderation, and clears carrier.

Receive-mode worker programs promiscuous and all-multicast states from interface flags and then unicast and multicast filter tables, triggered asynchronously when enabled and returning early without control support. VLAN add and delete each send their respective command and warn on failure while always reporting success.

MAC filter payload uses a shared allocation holding unicast entry count followed by that many addresses and then multicast entry count followed by that many addresses, with counts in device byte order sent as separate scatter elements.

Control path busy-waits for device response, assumes feature presence and descriptor bounds by fatal checks, transmit path treats descriptor setup failure as unexpected with warning and drop, VLAN and filter failures only warn, and backend resize may change size even on error so callers must re-query actual size.

Packet header offload uses distinct values for no segmentation, TCP over IP in distinct address families, and UDP segmentation, plus an ECN extension bit, and distinct flag values for checksum-needed versus data-valid states, with multi-byte fields in negotiated device byte order.

Control plane uses feature bits for control queue, MAC control, legacy MAC, version negotiation, VLAN filtering, receive control, multiqueue, scaling, and standby, with command families for MAC address and table, VLAN add and delete, receive promiscuous and all-multicast, queue-pair count, scaling versus hash setup, and link announce acknowledgement, plus a defined success status.

Affinity configuration delegates to transport support when present and otherwise reports success without action, and cleanup clears affinity for every send and receive queue when hints were previously set.
